meta.title: Pulse — The context AI agent that starts with meeting notes
meta.description: Pulse is the context AI agent that starts with meeting notes. Connect conversations, company knowledge, and decisions—from meeting preparation to the next action.

block2.reBuildingCategoryDefining: We're building a category-defining product in Tokyo, used daily by sales, CS and leadership teams. If your heart jumps a little when you read what's below, reach out.

block3.buildingGreatProductRare: Building a great product is rare. It takes a lot of care, love, and effort on the part of the people building it. We are a group of humans that care about each other, and make each other better.

heroL.turnMeetingNotesInto: Turn meeting notes into company knowledge
heroL.pulseCapturesWhatMatters: Pulse captures what matters and connects it to your teams' apps and AI tools, giving everyone the same context to work from. It works for all meeting types and platforms with built-in security and governance to reduce IT overhead.

block2.conversationDataNeverUsed: Your conversation data is never used to train AI models
block2.chooseWhereDataGoes: Choose where your data goes (like MCP, API and integrations)

block2.automaticNotificationsWhenPulse: Automatic notifications for when Pulse is being used
block2.adminsCanTurnNotifications: Admins can turn on notifications for everyone in the workspace
block2.spendLotTimeHard: We spend a lot of time on the hard parts about meeting notes—not just who said what, but why it was said and what it means for your team. It’s a small distinction, but it’s the one that makes notes worth reading instead of just forgetting.
block2.donTJustFeed: We don’t just feed transcripts into an AI model. We’ve built our own infrastructure to parse the nuances to capture intent, tone, and emphasis.
block2.builtWhereverConversationHappens: Built for wherever the conversation happens
block2.whetherSZoomTeams: Whether it’s Zoom, Teams, GMeet, in person, on a call, over Slack Huddle, or even from your watch, Pulse can take notes.

block3.mostImportantConversationsHappen: The most important conversations happen in meetings and it’s important to keep that information safe. Pulse meets the bar for every enterprise and offers built-in tools to make sure that participants are informed and admins have control of how their data is handled.
block3.controlSharingIntegrationsRetention: Control sharing, integrations and retention per workspace.
block3.samlSsoDirectorySync: SAML SSO and directory sync automate onboarding and offboarding.

during, and after a call

block3.pulseSpreadsBottomUp: Pulse spreads bottom-up: one person starts, colleagues see shared notes and follow. IT keeps that growth inside safe boundaries with admin controls.

block1.accountDetailsNameEmail: Account details (name, email, company), the notes and transcripts you create, app usage, and calendar events from connected calendars. Meeting audio is discarded after transcription and never stored.
block1.provideImproveServiceSupport: To provide and improve the Service, support you, keep it secure and comply with law. We do not train AI models on your data.
block1.useTranscriptionAiCloud: We use transcription, AI and cloud infrastructure providers to deliver the Service. The list is published on our subprocessor page.
block1.dataStoredEncryptedRegion: Data is stored encrypted in-region and retained until you delete it. Enterprise plans can set auto-deletion periods.
block1.encryptionRestTransitAccess: Encryption at rest and in transit, access controls, audit logs and staff training.
block1.mayRequestAccessCorrection: You may request access, correction, deletion or suspension of your personal data from within the app or by contacting us.
block1.websiteUsesCookiesConvenience: Our website uses cookies for convenience and analytics; disable them in your browser.
block1.changesPolicyWillPosted: Changes to this policy will be posted on our website.

heroL.securityPrivacyHowWorks: Security, privacy, and how it all works
heroL.securityPrivacyUtmostImportance: Your security and privacy are of utmost importance to us. Find the most important details below, followed by FAQs, and then links to all our terms and policies at the bottom of this page.
heroL.encourageSecurityVulnerabilityReports: We encourage security vulnerability reports and maintain a public Vulnerability Disclosure Policy with reporting guidelines and procedures.

block2.pulseAppDesktopMacos: Pulse is an app for Desktop (macOS and Windows), a lot like Apple Notes or Notion. It works with Google Workspace or Microsoft login and integrates with your calendar.
block2.haveManuallyStartPulse: You have to manually start Pulse for a meeting (it won't auto-join or auto-record anything). Pulse then accesses your microphone audio, and audio on your computer, and transcribes it. It does not add a bot to your video call.
block2.pulseWorksAnyMeeting: Pulse works with any meeting platform. Zoom, Meet, Teams, you name it.
block2.pulseUsesBestClass: Pulse uses best-in-class transcription providers and AI providers to summarize your meeting.
block2.doNotAllowThird: We do not allow third parties (like OpenAI or Anthropic) to use your data to train their AI models.
block2.pulseDoesNotTrain: Pulse does not train on your data either.
block2.pulseDoesnTStore: Pulse doesn't store the audio from meetings - it transcribes in real time and discards temporarily cached audio after processing. It only stores the transcript and any notes you provide from a call.
block2.controlWhoSeesNotes: You control who sees your notes
block2.userControlWhoSees: As a user, you control who sees your notes. Notes are private by default, until you choose to share them with others.
block2.canDeleteIndividualNotes: You can delete individual notes, or request deletion of all your data at any time.
block2.everythingStoredIndustryStandard: Everything stored in industry standard, encrypted infrastructure
block2.notesStoredRegionVirtual: Notes are stored in an in-region Virtual Private Cloud. They are encrypted at rest and in transit. They are backed up daily.
block2.reHereIfNeed: We're here if you need us
block2.ifHaveMoreQuestions: If you have more questions, please reach out to our team.
block2.rePreparingIndependentSoc: We're preparing an independent SOC 2 Type II audit of our security practices.
block2.reCommittedGdprAppi: We're committed to GDPR and APPI compliance and have a Data Processing Agreement available upon request.

block3.howDoesPulseSecure: How does Pulse secure customer data?
block3.encryptionRestTransitLeast: Encryption at rest and in transit, least-privilege access, audit logs and vulnerability scanning.
block3.doesPulseWorkLocally: Does Pulse work locally or send data to the cloud?
block3.audioCapturedLocallySent: Audio is captured locally and sent encrypted to the cloud only for transcription and summarization. Audio is not stored.
block3.howDoesPulseManage: How does Pulse manage security vulnerabilities?
block3.regularDependencyScanningPublic: Regular dependency scanning and a public vulnerability disclosure policy.
block3.annualThirdPartyPenetration: Annual third-party penetration tests are planned.
block3.doesPulseHaveAny: Does Pulse have any security certifications?
block3.soc2TypeIi: SOC 2 Type II is in progress; ISMS is planned.
block3.howCanIReport: How can I report security vulnerabilities?

contact.name: Name

contact.note: This opens a draft in your email app. Review it there before sending.
contact.direct: You can also email us directly.
contact.benefitOne: From pre-meeting briefs to notes and follow-ups.
contact.benefitTwo: No bot to invite. Use your usual meeting apps.
contact.benefitThree: Private notes. Share only the context you choose.
contact.processBody: Tell us about your team and goals. We will discuss a suitable trial, integrations, and any rollout or operational questions.

common.appsTitle: Connected to the tools behind your work.
common.noBot: No extra attendee in your call.
common.noBotBody: Capture audio on your device without inviting a bot. Let participants know you are recording, then focus on your conversation.
common.sync: Carry the outcome into your tools.
common.subject: Subject
common.question: Ask Pulse
common.example: From a conversation to the work
common.platformsBody: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams. Bring online and in-person conversations into your Pulse notes.
common.toolsHeading:
Bring your tools
into the conversation.
common.toolsBody: Prepare from your calendar. Connect the background in CRM, chat and documents, then carry meeting outcomes back into your work.
common.securityIntro: Keep personal notes separate from shared context. Choose who receives what, while keeping the background your team needs.
common.security0Body: Notes begin private. Choose what to share when you are ready.
common.security1Body: Pass selected context to your team or chosen recipients.
common.security2Body: Trace decisions and actions back to their conversations and sources.
common.security3Body: Review the meaning and sources of company terms before using them.
common.security4Body: Explain recording to participants before the conversation.
common.security5Body: Discuss your operating and information-management needs before rollout.
common.rolesTitle: For every role on your team.

sales.label: Sales
sales.headline:
Move the deal forward.
Keep the context.
sales.intro: Walk into every call with customer context. Turn the conversation into sourced notes, follow-up emails and CRM updates with Pulse for sales.
sales.briefBody: Bring together previous objections, decision-makers and open commitments from CRM and past conversations.
sales.briefText: Ken is considering a 20-person sales pilot. Director approval is required; pricing and security documents were requested.
sales.question: Who approves the pilot? What defines success?
sales.attentionBody: Keep your notes brief. Pulse connects them with the conversation and documents to capture customer needs, agreed terms and next steps.
sales.rough:
20 users / S plan
Ken → director approval
Quote by Friday
Pricing doc 18:42
sales.action: Taizo sends the quote and pilot terms by Friday.
sales.momentumBody: Turn commitments into work while the conversation is fresh. Prepare the follow-up and carry deal status, ownership and dates into CRM.
sales.followBody: Prepare an email that reflects the customer’s concerns and requested documents. Review it and send from the same workflow.
sales.mail: Thank you for today. Here are the pilot terms and quote for your 20-person team. Once your director approves, let’s confirm a start date.
sales.syncBody: Extract deal stage, pilot size and next steps from the conversation. Review the proposed changes and apply them without re-entering the same details.
sales.searchTitle:
Find the pattern
across your calls.
sales.searchBody: Which concerns keep coming up? Why are deals slowing down? Ask across conversations and get the context behind sales decisions, with sources.
sales.query: What is still unresolved in this deal?
sales.answerText: Director approval and the start date remain unconfirmed. After sending pricing, check approval status with Ken.
sales.exampleTitle:
Hand over more
than a deal stage.
sales.exampleBody: Why they are evaluating, whose approval is needed, and what you promised. The context that moves a deal survives a handoff.
sales.role0Body: Spend more time with customers, from preparation through follow-up.
sales.role1Body: See next steps and where a deal needs support, grounded in actual conversations.
sales.role2Body: Carry discovery needs and interests into a complete handoff.

customer-success.label: Customer Success
customer-success.headline:
Turn every check-in
into lasting trust.
customer-success.intro: Connect onboarding goals, everyday questions and customer commitments. Pulse helps CS teams follow through and keep everyone in context.
customer-success.briefBody: Bring onboarding goals, open actions and recent support conversations into your next customer check-in.
customer-success.briefText: One month after rollout: admin setup is complete, but the team workshop is still pending. Sato’s priority is consistent weekly use.
customer-success.question: What is blocking adoption? What should the next milestone be?
customer-success.attentionBody: Separate customer concerns from promised actions, retaining the evidence behind what they need.
customer-success.rough:
Admin setup done
Team workshop pending
Sato → gather attendees
Share guide next week
customer-success.decision: Run a workshop for the frontline team next week.
customer-success.action: CS sends the adoption guide and workshop dates.
customer-success.momentumBody: Turn every check-in into the next useful intervention, with follow-up, actions and customer context kept together.
customer-success.followBody: Send a clear recap of goals and commitments so everyone knows who is doing what before the next check-in.
customer-success.mail: Thank you for the review. Here is the adoption guide and a choice of workshop dates. Please let us know who will attend.
customer-success.syncBody: Update adoption status, next actions and ownership. Share the relevant background with sales and support.
customer-success.searchBody: What improved since the last review? Was the concern resolved? Ask past conversations for the background that keeps a relationship moving.
customer-success.query: What is still open in this customer’s adoption plan?
customer-success.answerText: Admin setup is complete. The team workshop and adoption guide remain open; Sato will coordinate attendees.
customer-success.exampleTitle:
Beyond a ticket.
A shared understanding.
customer-success.exampleBody: Keep the reason behind the rollout and the reality on the ground, so a new owner can continue supporting the customer with context.
customer-success.role0Body: Turn customer commitments and changes into useful support.
customer-success.role1Body: Keep rollout goals, setup status and open tasks together.
customer-success.role2Body: Understand customer context when prioritizing team support.

product.label: Product
product.headline:
Bring the user’s voice
into every decision.
product.intro: Connect interviews, specification discussions and development reviews. Pulse keeps user needs and product reasoning together.
product.briefBody: Prepare with previous feedback, your research hypothesis and the relevant specification.
product.briefText: The finance team cannot see where approvals are stuck. Today’s interview explores notification timing and how they use the overview.
product.question: Where does work stall? What is the current workaround?
product.attentionBody: Keep observations, interpretations and decisions distinct, with insights traceable to the original statement.
product.rough:
Cannot tell who owns approval
Asks in Slack every time
Wants owner in overview
Prototype next time
product.decision: Test showing the current approver and wait time in the overview.
product.action: PM documents the requirements for a test prototype.
product.momentumBody: Carry what you heard into what you build, through interview synthesis, team sharing and prepared development tasks.
product.followBody: Prepare a recap of the problem and next experiment for collaborators, without reconstructing the conversation from memory.
product.mail: The interview highlighted a lack of visibility into the current approver. We’ll test a prototype showing the owner and wait time.
product.syncBody: Carry requirements, rationale and test criteria into development tools, linked to the original user feedback.
product.searchTitle:
Find the reasoning
behind the roadmap.
product.searchBody: Why this specification? Which users had the problem? Search conversations and documents for the reasoning behind a decision.
product.query: What should we test first in the approval workflow?
product.answerText: Test visibility of the current approver and wait time. The hypothesis is that it reduces repeated Slack messages to find the owner.
product.exampleTitle:
Keep the why
between insight and spec.
product.exampleBody: Connect requests to problems, experiments and decisions. Give the team enough background to revisit the thinking, not just the specification.
product.role0Body: Connect hypotheses and evidence to the next experiment.
product.role1Body: Turn user conversations into traceable insights.
product.role2Body: Understand why a specification exists and which assumptions remain open.

marketing.label: Marketing
marketing.headline:
Keep the idea.
And the thinking behind it.
marketing.intro: Connect campaign planning, customer insights and agency discussions. Pulse keeps decisions and their rationale ready for execution.
marketing.briefBody: Prepare the campaign objective, previous concepts and unresolved constraints before the creative review.
marketing.briefText: The campaign focuses on adoption among existing customers. The team is considering customer stories supported by email and a webinar.
marketing.question: Who is the audience? What message should lead to action?
marketing.attentionBody: Separate ideas from commitments and retain the intent behind creative choices, including changes made in the discussion.
marketing.rough:
Existing customers first
Lead with customer stories
Email → webinar
First draft Wednesday
marketing.decision: Build a story-led campaign for existing customers.
marketing.action: Creative owner shares the outline by Wednesday.
marketing.momentumBody: Turn creative alignment into a starting point for execution, with a clear brief, owners and dates.
marketing.followBody: Send agencies and creators a clear recap of decisions and intent, including the context for people who missed the meeting.
marketing.mail: The campaign will use customer stories to drive adoption. Please share the outline by Wednesday so we can review the email-to-webinar journey.
marketing.syncBody: Carry objectives, agreed direction and deadlines into creative tasks, with matching context in chat and documents.
marketing.searchTitle:
Find the voice
behind your next campaign.
marketing.searchBody: What language resonated? Why was a direction chosen? Use past conversations to inform the next campaign.
marketing.query: Why are customer stories central to this campaign?
marketing.answerText: The goal is adoption. Practical customer stories lead into a webinar that helps customers picture how to use the product.
marketing.exampleTitle:
Share the direction.
Keep the intent.
marketing.exampleBody: Keep the objectives and discussion that a final asset cannot convey, so teams and agencies can maintain a consistent message.
marketing.role0Body: Keep objectives, channels and actions in one context.
marketing.role1Body: Use customer language and creative intent as evidence.
marketing.role2Body: Retain review changes and the reasoning behind creative choices.

operations.label: Operations
operations.headline:
Keep work moving
through every handoff.
operations.intro: Connect cross-functional reviews, process improvements and daily handoffs. Pulse preserves the context and ownership behind the work.
operations.briefBody: Prepare prior improvements, unresolved exceptions and ownership so the team can move beyond repeated status checks.
operations.briefText: Post-close order changes are increasing. Today’s review clarifies change history, approval steps and ownership between sales and administration.
operations.question: Where does work stall? Who owns exceptions?
operations.attentionBody: Separate issues, agreed procedures and open questions, retaining the meaning behind different teams’ terminology.
operations.rough:
More post-close changes
Need change history
Admin approves
Update playbook next week
operations.decision: Require administration approval and an audit trail for post-close changes.
operations.action: Administration updates the change procedure next week.
operations.momentumBody: Turn decisions into usable procedures, carrying owners, deadlines and exception rules into tools and operating knowledge.
operations.followBody: Share process changes and responsibilities across departments, with the background behind the handoff.
operations.mail: Post-close changes will require administration approval and a change log. Administration will update the procedure next week and share it with sales.
operations.syncBody: Carry decisions into operational records and playbooks, with ownership and deadlines visible from the same context.
operations.searchTitle:
Know why
the process works this way.
operations.searchBody: Why is this approval required? Who agreed to it? Find the basis for operational decisions in past conversations and playbooks.
operations.query: Why does administration need to approve post-close changes?
operations.answerText: The review agreed to retain the editor, time and before/after values as changes increase, managing approvals and history together.
operations.exampleTitle:
Hand over the process.
And the reasons behind it.
operations.exampleBody: When an exception occurs, revisit the conditions behind the rule. Give the next department the context to make a sound decision.
operations.role0Body: Carry process-review decisions into daily operations.
operations.role1Body: Keep approvals, exceptions and ownership with their rationale.
operations.role2Body: See commitments and dependencies across departments.

hr.label: HR
hr.headline:
Be present
for the people conversation.
hr.intro: Thoughtfully capture interviews, hiring alignment and onboarding discussions. Pulse helps HR teams follow through and share only the context they choose.
hr.briefBody: Review previous concerns and open actions so the person you are meeting does not have to repeat the same background.
hr.briefText: Week two: training is complete. The new hire wants to confirm a support contact and first assignment. Today focuses on how to work with the team.
hr.question: Is there a clear support contact? Is the next step understood?
hr.attentionBody: Focus on the person instead of exhaustive notes. Keep the conversation and agreed actions organized, and choose what to share.
hr.rough:
Training completed
Support contact unclear
Assign a mentor
1:1 next week
hr.decision: Assign a mentor and establish a weekly check-in.
hr.action: HR arranges the mentor introduction and next check-in.
hr.momentumBody: Keep the conversation moving into agreed support, useful resources and the next check-in for the person and their support team.
hr.followBody: Review and send the relevant recap and next steps without sharing the entire private meeting note.
hr.mail: Thank you for sharing your experience today. I’ll arrange the mentor introduction and send options for next week’s check-in. Please reach out with any questions.
hr.syncBody: Select the appropriate scope when updating onboarding actions. Keep personal meeting content separate from operational tasks.
hr.searchTitle:
Build the next step
on the last conversation.
hr.searchBody: Review previous concerns and commitments within the conversations you can access, so support can remain consistent.
hr.query: What should be prepared before the next check-in?
hr.answerText: Arrange the mentor introduction and next check-in. With training complete, prioritize a clear support contact and first assignment.
hr.exampleTitle:
The right context.
For the right support.
hr.exampleBody: Keep your meeting note private and pass agreed next steps to selected colleagues, balancing thoughtful conversations with coordinated support.
hr.role0Body: Maintain continuity in concerns and agreed support.
hr.role1Body: Share relevant meeting context and next steps with the right people.
hr.role2Body: Retain 1:1 commitments and topics for the next conversation.
